# Files — Vars

Var definitions are derived from `module.lowdefy.yaml`. Pass these via the `vars:` block in your app's `lowdefy.yaml` entry for this module.

## Summary

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `s3_region` |  |  | Yes | AWS region for S3 buckets (e.g., us-east-1, ca-central-1) |
| `log_events` | boolean | `true` |  | Log file upload/delete events via the events module |
| `max_file_size` | number | `26214400` |  | Largest upload in bytes (default 25 MB). upload-policy refuses a larger declared size, and the presigned policy carries the limit, so S3 refuses a larger upload. |
| `allowed_content_types` | array |  |  | Content types upload-policy accepts, such as [application/pdf, image/png]. Null (the default) accepts any type. |
| `access_check` | object |  |  | An app endpoint that decides who may work with a record's files. When set, list-files, upload-policy, save-file, download-file and delete-file each call it before they act, with { operation (list, upload, save, download or delete), entity_type, entity_id, file_id } (file_id is null for list and upload). Only { allowed: true } lets the operation go ahead; { allowed: false, message } stops it with that message, which the block shows. Unset, every signed-in member of the organization passes. A record may not be saved yet when it is asked: the activities module mints activity_id before the activity is saved, so files can be uploaded to a new activity, and the endpoint decides what to answer for a record it cannot find. |
| `components` | object |  |  | Component overrides: file_list (deprecated) |

## Nested var details

### `access_check`

An app endpoint that decides who may work with a record's files. When set, list-files, upload-policy, save-file, download-file and delete-file each call it before they act, with { operation (list, upload, save, download or delete), entity_type, entity_id, file_id } (file_id is null for list and upload). Only { allowed: true } lets the operation go ahead; { allowed: false, message } stops it with that message, which the block shows. Unset, every signed-in member of the organization passes. A record may not be saved yet when it is asked: the activities module mints activity_id before the activity is saved, so files can be uploaded to a new activity, and the endpoint decides what to answer for a record it cannot find.
